stem: Total number of Schedules in the Constitution is –
expl: There are 12 Schedules in our Constitution. Originally there were only 8 Schedules but 4 Schedules were added by Amendment Acts. The 9th Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment Act, 1951, related to the Validation of certain Acts and Regulations. The 10th Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985, which contains provisions of disqualification on the grounds of defection. The 11th Schedule was added by the 73rd Amendment in 1992 and it contains provisions of Panchayati Raj. 12th Schedule was added by the 74th Amendment Act, 1992 which contains provisions of the Municipalities, etc.

Consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution of India has 20 parts.
2. There are 390 Articles in the Constitution of India in all.
3. Ninth, Tenth, Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules were added to the Constitution of India by the Constitution (Amendment) Acts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: The Constitution of India has 22 Parts. Hence, statement (1) is incorrect. There are 395 Articles in the Constitution of India, therefore statement (2) is also incorrect. Ninth, Tenth, Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules were added to the Constitution of India by Constitutional (Amendment) Acts. Hence, statement (3) is correct. The Ninth Schedule added by the First Amendment Act, 1951 is related to land reforms and abolition of the Zamindari system, tenth schedule added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985, is related to Anti-defection provisions for members of Parliament and Members of the State Legislatures. By the Eleventh Schedule added through the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992; Panchayats have been given administrative control while in the Twelfth Schedule, added by the 74th Amendment Act, 1992 municipalities are given administrative control.

stem:
The Concurrent list of the Indian Constitution includes :
1. Trade and Commerce
2. Adulteration of Goods
3. Succession
Select the correct answer from the codes given below :
expl: “Adulteration of foodstuffs and other goods’ under entry-18 and ‘Succession’ under entry-5 are included in the Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution. The ‘Inter-State trade and commerce’ is in the Union List under entry 42. While, “Trade and commerce within the state’ is in the State List under entry-26, but it is subject to the entry-33 of the Concurrent List. The entry-33 of the concurrent list includes, Trade and Commerce in, and the production, supply and distribution of- (a) the products of any industry where the control of such industry by the Union is declared by the Parliament by law to be expedient in the public interest, and imported goods of the same kind as such products; (b) foodstuffs, including edible oilseeds and Oils; (c) Cattle fodder, including oilcakes and other concentrates; (d) raw cotton, whether ginned or unginned, and cotton seeds, and (e) raw jute. Hence, the trade and commerce of the above-mentioned goods is also included in the Concurrent List. Nevertheless, the U.P.P.S.C. in its answer-key, mentions option (d) as correct, because the Inter-State and With-in the State trade and commerce are mentioned under Union and State lists, respectively.

stem:
Consider the following subjects belonging to different lists of the constitution of India. Which of the following subjects belong to concurrent list?
1) Protection of wildlife
2) Income on Agriculture
3) Tax on Electricity consumption or sale
4) Price control Out of these:
expl: In the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, subjects are divided into three lists—Union List (List I), State List (List II) and Concurrent List (List III). Both Parliament and State Legislatures can make laws on subjects in the Concurrent List; however, if there is a conflict on a Concurrent List subject, the law made by Parliament prevails. • Protection of wild animals and birds – Concurrent List, Entry 17B. • Tax on agricultural income – State List, Entry 46. • Tax on consumption or sale of electricity – State List, Entry 53. • Price control – Concurrent List, Entry 34. Therefore, as per the options, the subjects in the Concurrent List are only (1) protection of wildlife and (4) price control.

stem: If a particular area is brought under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution of India, which one of the following statements best reflects the consequence of it?

options.label: c

options.label: d
options.text: The State having such areas would be declared a Special Category State.

expl: The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution defines scheduled areas as the areas defined so by the President of India. In India, there are 10 states having scheduled areas. With consultation of the governor of state, the president can alter, add or diminish the boundary of a scheduled area. The Governor can also repeal or amend any regulations with respect to the state having scheduled areas, but only with the assent of the President of India. Para (5) of the Fifth Schedule provides special power to the governor of the concerned state. Under this power, he prevents the transfer of land from tribal people to non-tribal people.

stem:
With reference to ‘Scheduled Areas’ in India, consider the following statements :
1. Within a State, the notification of an area as Scheduled Area takes place through an Order of the President.
2. The largest administrative unit forming the Scheduled Area is the District and the lowest is the cluster of villages in the Block.
3. The Chief Ministers of the concerned States are required to submit annual reports to the Union Home Ministry on the administration of Scheduled Areas in the States. How many of the above statements are correct?
expl: Part X of the Constitution, Article 244, provides for a unique administrative structure for some places classified as "scheduled areas" and "tribal areas." As per Part C of the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution, the expression Scheduled Areas means such areas as the President may, by order, declare to be Scheduled Areas. The largest administrative unit forming the scheduled areas is the district and the cluster of villages in the block is the lowest. Hence, statements 1 and 2 are correct. At present, 10 states of India have scheduled areas. These are: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Rajasthan. The governor has a special responsibility regarding such areas. He has to submit a report to the president regarding the administration of such areas, annually or whenever so required by the President. Hence statement 3 is not correct.

stem:
Consider the following statements : With reference to the Constitution of India, if an area in a State is declared as Scheduled Area under the Fifth Schedule
I. the State Government loses its executive power in such areas and a local body assumes total administration.
II. the Union Government can take over the total administration of such areas under certain circumstances on the recommendations of the Governor
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: The executive power of a State, subject to the provisions of the Fifth Schedule, extends to the Scheduled Areas as well. Declaring an area as a Scheduled Area under the Fifth Schedule does not mean that the State Government loses its executive power; it continues to exercise executive authority there. Neither the Fifth Schedule nor Article 339 contains any provision that, on the recommendation of the Governor, the Central Government can, in certain circumstances, take over the entire administration of the Scheduled Areas. Hence, Statement II is also incorrect.
